 The Sixers will start Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, LeBron James, Dean Wade, and Joel Embiid against the Knicks
 Jaylen Brown (knee) is out tonight, so Dean Wade will take his spot in the starting lineup. Even if heavy minutes, Dean Wade is not a fantasy add unless it’s in deeper leagues. With one less high usage guy in the starting lineup, LeBron and VJ might get a bump in production tonight.

 Tyrese Maxey

 Tyrese Maxey scores 27 points (8-of-18 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), five rebounds, four assists, a steal, and three 3-pointers on Wednesday in win over the Pacers. 
 It was a bad night for Maxey’s standards up until he took over in the fourth quarter and carried the 76ers to a win with 17 fourth quarter points. He wasn’t taking many shots during most of the game until he started to get going, which is great if you own him as a fantasy manager. He’s established himself as the best player on the team and any worries about Maxey’s production going down should subside. 
 Tyrese Maxey 
 PHI 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Tyrese Maxey (head) finished Sunday’s loss to the Pistons with 29 points (11-of-24 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), five rebounds, four assists, three steals, one block and one three-pointer. 
 Maxey and the 76ers were playing their third game in four days. With LeBron James (Saturday) and Joel Embiid (Sunday) each missing a game, the 76ers’ star point guard had to shoulder a heavier workload. Despite that, Maxey still recorded an efficient stat line to end Week 1. There was an injury scare when he collided with Detroit’s John Collins in the fourth quarter, but Maxey was fine. Philadelphia plays three games in Week 2, starting with the Pacers on Wednesday. 
 Tyrese Maxey 
 PHI 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Tyrese Maxey recorded 26 points (9-of-22 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, four assists and four three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Bucks. 
 Maxey finished the first and third quarters of Saturday’s win with buzzer-beaters, with one being a half-court shot. The 76ers’ point guard has scored at least 26 points in all three games this season, attempting 19 shots or more in each. Neither Maxey’s usage nor his production has suffered so far, and he’s especially well-positioned to feast in back-to-backs. LeBron James sat out Saturday’s game, and Joel Embiid won’t play on Sunday against the Pistons, which should be good news for those rostering Maxey. 
 Tyrese Maxey 
 PHI 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Tyrese Maxey finished Thursday’s win over the Cavaliers with 32 points (12-of-23 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, two steals and two three-pointers. 
 The 76ers pulled off one of the biggest comebacks in franchise history on Thursday, rallying from a 29-point deficit to win 114-106 in their home opener. Maxey was Philadelphia’s most consistent offensive player, and his defense on James Harden also played a role. Harden scored 10 points in the second half but also recorded more turnovers (four) than assists (two). If the first two games indicate what’s to come, Maxey will be the 76ers’ first offensive option. Given his first-round ADP, that’s great news for fantasy managers. 
 Tyrese Maxey 
 PHI 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Tyrese Maxey led the 76ers with 28 points (9-of-19 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, three steals, three blocks and two three-pointers in a 106-100 win over the Knicks on Tuesday. 
 Even with all the roster changes, this is still going to be Maxey’s team. While spoiling the Knicks’ ring night, he was assertive on both ends of the floor and truly stuffed the stat sheet. Having more playmaking and scoring threats around him will only make things easier on him, and it’s clear he’s not going to have to sacrifice much volume. Those who took Maxey at the end of the first round in fantasy drafts may end up reaping some major rewards.

 Tyrese Maxey managed just eight points (2-of-10 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block over 18 minutes in Saturday’s preseason loss to the Celtics. 
 Maxey has tormented the Celtics in recent years, but he had an off-night from a shooting standpoint, going just 1-of-6 from three-point range as the 76ers were run off the floor by Boston’s relentless bench. The 25-year-old is the force multiplier that will make Philadelphia’s star-studded mix functional this season. It might take some time for all of the piece to settle into the correct slots, but Maxey is going to be the biggest constant from the get-go as the straw that stirs the metaphorical drink.

 Guard 
 #0 
 Tyrese Maxey recorded 14 points (5-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, two assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Thursday’s exhibition against the Nets. 
 Back on the floor after sitting out Monday’s preseason opener against the Knicks, Maxey logged 19 minutes on Thursday. With LeBron James on the court as well, the third-team All-NBA point guard spent more time off the ball. Maxey’s assist production could take a hit this season, but he may make up for it with more scoring. Either way, anyone who drafts him shouldn’t regret it. 
 Jalen Duren 
 DET 
 Center 
 #0 
 Jalen Duren, Chet Holmgren, Jalen Johnson, Tyrese Maxey and Jamal Murray were named third-team All-NBA on Sunday. 
 All five third-team selections were named All-NBA for the first time in their respective careers on Sunday. Duren’s selection may be the most impactful, as he’ll hit restricted free agency next month. The All-NBA selection makes him eligible for a max deal worth up to $287 million over five years. However, given his struggles during the postseason and the Pistons’ need to also address Ausar Thompson’s future, Duren may not strike it that rich this summer. Especially with other teams unable to offer a deal on par with what the Pistons can. 
 Tyrese Maxey 
 PHI 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Tyrese Maxey recorded 17 points (6-of-16 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, four assists and one three-pointer in Sunday’s Game 4 loss to the Knicks. 
 A standout performer for most of this season, Maxey appeared to be a shell of himself in the second round. He had just one 20-point game in the four-game sweep, with the combination of the Knicks’ defense, specifically Mikal Bridges, and an injured right pinky finger being too much to overcome. Maxey will take some heat for his play in this series, and rightfully so. But there should be no concern from fantasy managers regarding the point guard’s outlook for 2026-27. Maxey provided first-round per-game value this season, and his emergence makes him a player who should come off the board in the first round of drafts next fall. 
 Tyrese Maxey 
 PHI 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Tyrese Maxey finished Friday’s Game 3 loss to the Knicks with 17 points (8-of-12 FGs), two rebounds, seven assists, one steal and one three-pointer. 
 While Maxey shot the ball well on Friday, he was far too deferential on offense in a game the 76ers needed to win. There were too many moments in which the point guard continued to swing the ball instead of attacking the closeout and getting downhill. While that may have been the “right play,” the 76ers need a more aggressive Maxey on offense to have any chance, especially when considering the team’s lack of depth. To force a Game 5, Philadelphia needs Maxey to be in “takeover mode” from the start of Sunday’s Game 4.

 Ausar Thompson had 11 points (5-of-9 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, six assists, and two steals on Friday. 
 Ausar has been awesome in category leagues if you need good out of position rebounds and assists.  Tre Jones finished Friday’s loss to the Celtics with 12 points (4-of-10 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, four steals and one block.
 In his usual role backing up Josh Giddey (13/4/5 with two three-pointers), Jones played 20 minutes on Friday. That didn’t prevent him from providing solid category-league value, especially in steals. The four pilfers were one shy of his career-high, and the Bulls guard also managed to block a shot. Regardless of what Giddey does on any given night, Jones is worth rostering in deep leagues.

 Duncan Robinson put up 17 points (5-of-11 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), four rebounds, two assists, three steals, and two 3-pointers in win on Friday. 
 Robinson has been on an absolute tear to start the season. He’s been the biggest beneficiary of Tobias Harris leaving the team in terms of scoring and he’s given fantasy owners a real boost in the 3-point category. If he’s available in your league, he’s worth grabbing in most redraft leagues, but understand that unless you need some 3’s or points, he doesn’t do much else.

 Ron Holland in 22 minutes, got 18 points (6-of-10 FGs, 4-of-7 FTs), three rebounds, two assists, four steals, a block, and two 3-pointers in 110-94 win over the Nets. 
 Ron Holland was a big reason that this game got so out of and in the second half. He hit his shots and he was aggressive with his defense. He got you four steals which would’ve been a massive boost in deeper leagues. We’ll see if he stays on this team long term, but tonight was one of the nights where you can see the fantasy profile if he ever gets a starting role.

 Naz Reid scored 12 points (5-of-17 FGs, 0-of-2 FTs), 11 rebounds, an assist, three steals, and two 3-pointers in 31 minutes. 
 Naz Reid got the start after being benched in the second half of last game, but it looks to be a one game thing. While he didn’t fill up the box score, he still filled up the box score despite it, but it wasn’t a good performance from the Hornets as a whole. If you have Naz, be patient and don’t overreact. He won’t likely go shoot 29.4% from the field and 25% from three very often.

 Brandon Miller scored 19 points (7-of-24 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, a steal, a block, and three 3-pointers in 95-79 loss to Wizards. 
 After having three straight good games in a row against the Heat, Wizards, and Pistons, he had another bad game. The Wizards did much better on containing Miller and Naz Reid in this game which allowed them to come away with a win against them. Don’t panic after he gave you several good games and he’ll have an opportunity to have a bounce back game tomorrow against the 76ers. The Hornets will not likely shoot 29.7% from the field tomorrow either.

 AJ Dybantsa in his second career game had 17 points (5-of-11 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), eight rebounds, an assist, two steals, and a three in win over the Hornets. 
 AJ has made an effort to work on his defense and his off-ball ability, and it has paid off in a big way. He hasn’t been nearly as ball dominant as he was in college, and the shot looks much better than it was at BYU. He’s already the third best player on the team and he will continue to climb up the hierarchy. Outside of Trae, AD, and AJ tonight, it was pretty rough from the Wizards tonight despite the win.

 Anthony Davis had himself a night with 25 points (8-of-18 FGs, 9-of-10 FTs), 13 rebounds, one assist, one steal, and a block on Friday in win. 
 Anthony Davis has imposed his will on the Hornets centers in this game, and they couldn’t do much to stop him. The defense on the big men was good, and he got to the line frequently. It was another great performance from AD and his value should be stable barring injury. The Wizards are winning and he’s a big reason for that. If you’re worried about the injuries, it might be worth exploring the market, but it’s also likely everyone else is just as scared about him.
